name: Greetings
description: The personality x standing matrix that decides what a villager says when you walk up (DESIGN §5.9). Each row lists the conditions under which it may be said; the most specific matching row wins, with weight breaking ties. Every row holds several lines so the same shopkeeper does not greet you identically twice. Tokens: {player}, {title}, {npc}, {place}, {region}.

lines: Aye.
Morning. Or afternoon. One of them.
Yes?
Mind the step there, it's older than the house.
Oh good, a new face. Sit down, you won't believe what the miller's done.
You're not from the lane, are you. Go on, then. Where from?
I'll tell you something, and then you tell me something. That's how it works here.
Mm.
Aye. Weather's weather.
Oh — hello. Sorry. Hello.
I wasn't — did you want something? It's fine if you do.
You walk quietly. That's not a complaint. It nearly is.
You look like you've walked a way. Sit or don't.
If you're trouble, be quick about it. I've bread in the oven.
Come on in. The dog bites, but only the once.
You'll want something. They always want something.
I am busy and important and you may have a moment of it.
Speak up, then. I've a name to keep up.
Don't mind me. Nobody else does, and we get on fine.
Hello. There's tea if you want it. It's mostly hot.
Oh, you don't want to talk to me, I only do the fences.
Buying or selling? Those are the two things there are.
Everything's for sale. Some of it's even mine.
Marks first, friendliness after. That's not rudeness, that's bookkeeping.
You look half-starved. Sit down before you fall down.
Take an apple. No, take it, they'll only go over.
Come in out of it. Whatever it is, it keeps better indoors.
Keep warm, stranger. Say somebody's name today.
The hearth's lit and there's a place at it. That's all any of it is.
You've the look of somebody the world's forgotten to introduce itself to.
Let me guess. You're here to fix something and it'll cost us.
New face. New face means news, and news has never once been good.
Say what you want plainly and I'll say no plainly and we'll both save an hour.
Someone said your name in here last week. Only the once, mind.
You're the one from — no. No, it's gone. But you're the one.
I know your face from somebody else's mouth.
You're {player}! I told them you were real and they laughed at me.
I've been hearing about you in the half-sentences people use when they're not sure.
{player}. Aye, I know the name.
Well. {player} {title}, in my doorway. My mother would have swept.
You'll not need introducing round here any more.
{player}, is it. I'll believe half of it and still be impressed, which annoys me.
Famous, are we. Does famous pay for ale? It does not.
{player} {title}. They've a verse about you at the inn and two of the rhymes are a crime.
You're spoken of. Do you know what that does to a village? It warms it. Sit down.
There's children playing at being you in the lane. Badly.
I knew you before they did. I want that written down somewhere.
{title}, they're calling you. I shall use it and I shall be the first.
{player} {title}. I'll tell my grandchildren where I was standing.
They say your name at the Hearthstone to keep the stone warm. I've heard them do it.
You've got the look of somebody the world has decided to keep. Sit. Please.
There are four or five people whose names hold a village up. You're one, {title}.
Be careful what you are remembered for. It sets, like plaster.
There's a kindness that comes off you. My cat's noticed it and my cat notices nothing.
You've the warm look. Whatever you've been doing, do more of it.
Door's open to you. It isn't for everyone.
Ha! Good, another one of us. Take the chair by the fire, you've earned the good chair.
They say when you sleep somewhere the fire needs less wood. I don't believe it. I half believe it.
Bless you, and I don't say that. Ask anyone.
You're a cold one, aren't you. Not rude. Cold.
Keep your distance and we'll keep being friendly.
Something's gone quiet in you. That's not a judgement, it's a description.
Quiet-eyed. That's what my mother would have called you, and then locked the door.
You'll want to move along. The children are at the window.
I'll talk to you. I'd rather do it out here, though.
Go on. Go on, now. There's nothing for you here and we both know why.
Hollow. Somebody had to say it and it might as well be me, from behind this door.
You put the fire out just standing near it. Please go.
Please — I've nothing, I've said nothing about you to anyone —
I'm going inside now. I'm going inside.
I know what you are and I'm still standing here. Say your piece.
You don't frighten me. You do frighten my neighbours, and that's worse.
You've a price on you, haven't you. Small one. Still a price.
The Watch were asking after somebody with your walk.
You shouldn't be standing in daylight, you. Not with what's on your head.
I've seen the notice. I've seen the number on the notice. Go.
If anyone asks, you came in the back and I was asleep.
I saw what you did. I haven't slept right since, and here you are saying hello.
Don't. Whatever it is you want, don't. I know.
You've a nerve, coming to me with a greeting.
They're saying there was blood at the door and your name in the same breath.
Nobody in this street will write it down, but everybody in this street has said it.
The thing under the hill has a killer and the killer is standing in my shop. Marvellous day.
We heard. We all heard. The fiddler's already ruined it with a tune.
You brought that child home. Whatever else you are, you brought that child home.
There's a family three doors up who will not let you pay for anything ever again.
Things go missing when you're about, they say. I'm just repeating it. I'm also counting the spoons.
Not accusing. Just — everything's where I can see it, that's all.
They say you had one at your mercy and let them walk. That's rarer than the killing.
Soft, some are calling it. I'd call it something else, but not loudly.
Warden. There's a lamp lit at the Rest for you, as always.
Your boots are muddy and the Wardens' boots are muddy. I'm just saying.
Any names to add? No? Good. Good.
Roll-Warden. We'd a hamlet go quiet up the valley. You'll want to hear it from Hesk.
They say you can name a Hearthstone now. That's not a small thing to be able to do.
One of the Circle. Say something loud, then. That's the joke. We all make it.
Careful with the words in here, we've only the one roof.
I don't know you. That's the correct answer and I'll give it again if anyone asks.
Evening. Nothing's happened here and nobody's been in.
Bell-sworn. You'll want the grey soup, everyone does, nobody knows why.
You keep the vigil, then. Somebody should and it's never going to be me.
The Guild speaks well of you, which costs them nothing, so it must be true.
Your credit's good in three streets. Don't spend that carelessly.
The Moot remembers you, which is the only currency up here.
You've a name in Kharrow. Carry it carefully, it's heavier than it looks.
You waited, last time. People notice waiting.
The boardwalk's yours. Mind the third plank, it's a liar.
You take only what you need. We watched. We always watch.
The Wold's quiet with you in it. That's as much as we say to anyone.
We know what you did to ours. Say your piece from there.
You've friends here. None of them are in this room.
It's late for walking about. Not wrong. Late.
Everything's shut but me and I'm shutting.
Whatever it is, could it be it in the morning?
Who's — oh. Oh, it's you. Don't do that at this hour.
I nearly hit you with a pan. I want you to know how close it was.
You're up with the larks and the liars.
Bread's not out yet. Nothing's out yet. I'm barely out yet.
Morning. First one I've said today, so mind how you answer it.
Long day, was it. They're all long now.
Come in, the light's going and the fire isn't.
That's the last of the sun. Say what you came to say by it.
That thing you're wearing. Take it off before you come further in. Please.
My grandmother had a word for what's on your shoulders and I won't repeat it indoors.
Warden's colours. Right. What's gone wrong, then?
Lamp on your coat. That's either very good news or very bad.
Look at the cloth on you. Tollmere, is it? It's always Tollmere.
You'll not want to lean on anything in here, dressed like that.
There's blood on you. I'm going to carry on as if there isn't.
Whatever that is down your front, it is not coming into my kitchen.
Marsh indigo. You've been out to the stilts, then. How's the water sitting?
That dye's Isseva's and nobody else's. Did you wait properly for it?
Don't know you.
You'll be passing through, then. Everyone is, lately.
No name on you yet. Give it time, this lot will find one.
There you are! I was only saying about you this morning.
Ah, good. Somebody I actually want to see.
Sit down, sit down. There's a pie and you're having some of it.
You again.
I've nothing for you and I'd like the doorway back.
We are not friends. I want that established before you start.
